note.en: Group one holds words built on the same wind element, including one that looks unrelated; group two holds other names for air in motion and for the power it carries.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 wind 成分的词，其中包括一个看似无关的词；第二组是流动空气及其所带动力 的其他名称。

entries.definition: The noun for moving air and the verb for twisting or making breathless are different words that happen to share a spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 指流动空气的名词与指缠绕或使喘不过气的动词是两个不同的词，只是拼写相同。

entries.definition: From Old Norse vindauga 'wind eye', a real compound of wind and eye, so it is a distant relative of wind energy.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古诺尔斯语 vindauga「风眼」，是 wind 与 eye 的真实复合，因此与 wind energy 有远亲关系。

entries.definition: A mill driven by wind; it names the machine, while wind energy names the input.
entries.definitionCN: 由风驱动的磨坊；它指机器，而 wind energy 指输入。

entries.definition: From windan 'to twist', a verb of different origin; a winding road has nothing to do with air.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 windan「缠绕」，是另一来源的动词；蜿蜒的路与空气无关。

entries.definition: Usually the electrical output of wind systems, where wind energy can also mean the resource or the mechanical input.
entries.definitionCN: 通常指风力系统的电力输出，而 wind energy 也可指资源或机械输入。

entries.definition: A gentle wind, especially one felt as pleasant; it is a kind of wind, not a form of power.
entries.definitionCN: 轻风，尤指令人舒适的风；它是风的一种，不是一种动力。

entries.definition: The movement of air around or through an object, used in engineering rather than in energy accounting.
entries.definitionCN: 空气绕过或穿过物体的运动，用于工程语境而非能源核算。

entries.definition: The wider class that includes wind, solar, water and biomass; wind energy is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的类别，包含风能、太阳能、水能与生物质能；风能是其中一员。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: wind + energy: the phrase simply names the moving air and the work it can do.
normal.cn: wind + energy：短语直接点名流动的空气与它能做的功。

normal.en: The family runs wind, windy, windmill, wind farm, wind turbine, wind power.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 wind、windy、windmill、wind farm、wind turbine、wind power。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the industry: wind energy capacity, wind energy sector, wind energy potential.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出产业义：风能装机容量、风能行业、风能潜力。

normal.en: Latin ventus 'wind' shares the same Indo-European root as English wind.
normal.cn: 拉丁 ventus「风」与英语 wind 共享同一印欧词根。

normal.en: The old mill is the physical ancestor of the turbine: both capture wind energy with a spinning shaft.
normal.cn: 老磨坊是涡轮机的物理祖先：两者都用旋转轴捕获风能。

abstract.en: Picture a sail that asks the sky for nothing but a push.
abstract.cn: 想象一张帆，只向天空要一阵推力，别无所求。

abstract.en: Picture a field of white trees whose leaves never stop turning.
abstract.cn: 想象一片白色树林，叶子从不停下转动。

abstract.en: Picture a river you cannot see, yet its current turns the wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象一条看不见的河，水流却在转动轮子。

examples.en: The island meets half its demand with wind energy.
examples.cn: 这座岛用风能满足一半需求。

examples.en: Wind energy cannot be stored cheaply without batteries.
examples.cn: 没有电池，风能难以低成本储存。

examples.en: The textbook explains how wind energy drives a generator.
examples.cn: 这本教材讲解风能如何驱动发电机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「wind（风）+ energy（能量）」——风带来的能量 → 风能

root: wind 为英语本族词，源自原始日耳曼语 windaz，更上溯到意为「吹」的印欧词根（重构形式），与拉丁 ventus「风」同根；energy 来自希腊 energeia「活动」= en-「在内」+ ergon「工作」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one flow: air moves, blades turn, a shaft spins, current or mechanical work leaves, and the same flow is then counted as a resource, an industry, a physical quantity, an emblem and a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条流程展开：空气流动、叶片转动、轴旋转、电流或机械功输出，随后同一流动被计为资源、产业、物理量、象征与比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white blades on a ridge turning wind into a spinning shaft.
core.cn: 核心意象：山脊上的白色叶片把风变成旋转的轴。

branches.en: PHYSICAL FLOW: moving air carries kinetic energy, whether measured in a formula or felt on a ridge.
branches.cn: 物理流动：流动空气携带动能，无论用公式测量还是在山脊上感受。

branches.en: CONVERTED OUTPUT: the turning shaft yields electric current or direct mechanical work.
branches.cn: 转换输出：旋转的轴产生电流或直接的机械功。

branches.en: RESOURCE: the wind over a site is surveyed and entered into plans.
branches.cn: 资源：某地的风被测绘并计入规划。

branches.en: INDUSTRY: subsidies, permits and markets turn the flow into a sector.
branches.cn: 产业：补贴、许可与市场把这一流动变成行业。

branches.en: EMBLEM AND METAPHOR: the phrase stands for clean politics, then for any momentum that can be redirected.
branches.cn: 象征与比喻：短语代表清洁政治，再引申为任何可被改向的势头。

intro.en: Wind energy combines a native Germanic noun with a Greek-derived noun. The native element still forms everyday compounds, while the Greek element forms the scientific vocabulary of work and power.
intro.cn: wind energy 把一个日耳曼本族名词与一个希腊来源名词组合起来。本族成分仍构成日常复合词，希腊成分则构成工作与动力的科学词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin ventus 'wind' is a distant relative of English wind; Latin turbo gives turbine, and Greek energeia gives energy, energetic and energize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ventus「风」是英语 wind 的远亲；拉丁 turbo 衍生 turbine，希腊 energeia 衍生 energy、energetic 与 energize。

items.example: A windy ridge suits a turbine.
items.exampleCN: 多风的山脊适合建风机。

items.example: The coast is windy in spring.
The Greek noun supplied the term for work-capacity.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词提供了表示做功能力的术语。

items.example: The blades convert moving air into energy.
items.exampleCN: 叶片把流动空气转化成能量。

items.example: The gust was energetic enough to bend the mast.
items.exampleCN: 那阵风强得足以吹弯桅杆。

items.meaning: a machine driven by a moving fluid
items.meaningCN: 由流动流体驱动的机器；涡轮机
items.example: A turbine converts flow into rotation.
items.exampleCN: 涡轮机把流动转化为旋转。

items.meaningCN: 流动空气供给的动力；风能
items.example: A row of turbines turns wind energy into household current.
items.exampleCN: 一排风机把风能变成家庭用电。

latinEntries.structure: energia, -ae (f., first declension; from Greek energeia)

definition_zh: 具有仪式特征的；程式化到近乎机械的
definition_en: done in the manner of a rite, especially in a fixed or exaggeratedly formal way
core_image: 后台的化妆镜前摆着一排面具，演员按固定顺序逐一戴上
scene: 后台的化妆镜前摆着一排面具，演员按固定顺序逐一戴上。 The dancers moved with a ritualistic slowness that made every gesture feel ancient.
sceneCN: 这里 ritualistic 指「带有仪式特征的」（第 1 个义项：动作按仪轨般的方式完成）；句意为舞者以仪式般缓慢的动作移动，使每个手势都显得古老。可辨识物件：化妆镜、面具、戏服、幕布。

senses.title: Having the character of a rite
senses.definition: carried out with the ordered, solemn quality of a religious or formal rite
senses.definitionCN: 以宗教或正式仪式的有序、庄严方式完成
senses.example: The dancers moved with a ritualistic slowness that made every gesture feel ancient.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者以仪式般缓慢的动作移动，使每个手势都显得古老。
senses.why: ritual plus -istic means 'in the manner of a rite', so the adjective describes style rather than belief.
senses.whyCN: ritual 加 -istic 意为「以仪式的方式」，因此这个形容词描述风格而非信仰。

senses.title: Fixed to the point of being mechanical
senses.definition: repeated so exactly that the action looks automatic rather than alive
senses.definitionCN: 重复得过于精确，以致动作显得自动而非鲜活
senses.example: His ritualistic handshake never varied by a single degree.
senses.exampleCN: 他那仪式化的握手连角度都从不改变。
senses.why: a rite is fixed by definition, and the adjective turns that fixity into a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 仪式按定义就是固定的，这个形容词把这种固定变成了批评。

senses.title: Strictly following a religious order
senses.definition: observing every prescribed word and gesture of worship without deviation
senses.definitionCN: 不偏差地遵守礼拜中每一句规定言辞与动作
senses.example: The sect remained ritualistic long after the town had loosened.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上早已松弛下来，这个教派却仍严守仪轨。
senses.why: the adjective is neutral or admiring here: exactness is taken as faithfulness.
senses.whyCN: 此处形容词是中性的甚至赞许的：精确被视为虔诚。

senses.title: Compulsive repetition in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中的仪式化重复行为
senses.definition: describing repeated acts performed to hold off anxiety rather than to worship
senses.definitionCN: 指为抵挡焦虑而非为敬拜而重复执行的动作
senses.example: The report described ritualistic checking that occupied two hours a day.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了一种每天占用两小时的仪式化检查。
senses.why: psychology borrowed the word because compulsion and rite share the same visible shape.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用这个词，因为强迫行为与仪式在外形上一致。

senses.title: Stylized ritual quality in art
senses.titleCN: 艺术表演中的仪式性风格
senses.definition: describing theatre, dance or film that uses slow, formal, repeated movement
senses.definitionCN: 描述使用缓慢、正式、重复动作的戏剧、舞蹈或电影
senses.example: Critics praised the ritualistic staging of the funeral scene.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞葬礼一场的仪式化舞台处理。
senses.why: art borrows the authority of rites to make ordinary action feel weighty.
senses.whyCN: 艺术借仪式的权威，让寻常动作显得沉重。

senses.title: Ceremonial steps inside an organization
senses.titleCN: 组织流程中的仪式化环节
senses.definition: describing formal procedures that a group performs as much for identity as for results
senses.definitionCN: 描述群体为身份认同而非仅为结果而执行的形式化程序
senses.example: The firm's ritualistic approval chain delayed every small purchase.
senses.exampleCN: 公司仪式化的审批链让每笔小额采购都被拖延。
senses.why: organizations invent rites to make hierarchy visible, and the adjective names the cost.
senses.whyCN: 组织发明仪式以让层级可见，这个形容词则指出其代价。

senses.title: Mere going through the motions
senses.definition: done for appearance only, with the original purpose emptied out
senses.definitionCN: 只为外观而做，原初目的已被掏空
senses.example: The hearing was a ritualistic gesture with no real power.
senses.exampleCN: 那场听证只是走个仪式，并无实权。
senses.why: when form survives meaning, the word turns ironic, close to 'merely formal'.
senses.whyCN: 当形式比意义活得久，这个词就转为讽刺，近似「只是形式上」。

senses.title: Display behaviour in animal studies
senses.titleCN: 动物行为学中的仪式化展示
senses.definition: describing courtship or threat displays that are repeated in a fixed sequence
senses.definitionCN: 描述按固定序列重复的求偶或威吓展示
senses.example: Ethologists recorded the ritualistic display of the male bird.
senses.exampleCN: 动物行为学家记录了雄鸟的仪式化展示。
senses.why: animal behaviour uses the same word because fixed display serves as a signal, like a rite.
senses.whyCN: 动物行为学使用同一个词，因为固定展示像仪式一样充当信号。

intro.en: Ritualistic is English ritual plus the suffix -istic, which came through Latin from Greek -istikos 'in the manner of'. Ritual itself comes from Latin ritus 'rite'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ritualistic 是英语 ritual 加后缀 -istic，后者经拉丁语来自希腊 -istikos「以……方式」。ritual 本身来自拉丁 ritus「仪式」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ritus meant 'a rite, a religious ceremony'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and the suggested link to a Vedic word for fixed order is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: ritus 意为「仪式、宗教典礼」。其更深来源不确定，把它与吠陀语中「固定秩序」一词相联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ritus plus -alis gave ritualis 'relating to rites', the adjective that English borrowed as ritual.
items.cn: ritus 加 -alis 构成 ritualis「与仪式有关的」，英语借入后作 ritual。

items.en: The suffix -istikos formed adjectives of manner; Latin took it as -isticus, and French and English shortened it to -istic.
items.cn: 后缀 -istikos 构成表方式的形容词；拉丁语吸收为 -isticus，法语与英语再缩短为 -istic。

items.en: English ritualistic first described church parties devoted to elaborate rites in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语 ritualistic 在十九世纪最早用来描述热衷繁复礼仪的教会派别。

items.en: Psychology, art criticism and animal behaviour later took the adjective for compulsive, stylized and display behaviour.
items.cn: 心理学、艺术批评与动物行为研究后来用这个形容词指强迫性、风格化与展示性行为。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of the psychological sense is not recorded, and the pre-Latin origin of ritus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：心理学义没有确切的最早书证；ritus 在拉丁语之前的来源仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same stem; group two holds adjectives for related kinds of formality.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一词干的词；第二组是表示相关形式化程度的形容词。

entries.definition: The rite itself or a plain adjective meaning 'of a rite'; ritualistic adds the idea of manner or excess.
entries.definitionCN: 指仪式本身，或意为「仪式的」的普通形容词；ritualistic 另带方式或过度的意味。

entries.definition: Attachment to rites as a system, or the study of them; it names a tendency, not a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指对仪式体系的依附或对它的研究；它指倾向，而非方式。

entries.definition: A single prescribed ceremony; the adjective never means 'a ceremony'.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个规定的典礼；这个形容词从不表示「一场典礼」。

entries.definition: The adverb form, used of performing an act in a rite-like manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，指以仪式般的方式完成某动作。

entries.definition: Relating to an official ceremony; it points to the occasion and its dignity.
entries.definitionCN: 指与正式典礼有关，指向场合及其庄重。

entries.definition: Overly polite and formal in manner, especially between people.
entries.definitionCN: 指举止过分客气正式，尤指人际之间。

entries.definition: Following accepted rules of style; ritualistic is narrower and points to rite-like repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵循公认的形式规则；ritualistic 更窄，指向仪式般的重复。

entries.definition: Carried out as a duty with little interest; ritualistic can imply the same hollowness but stresses form.
entries.definitionCN: 指当作义务草草完成；ritualistic 也可含同样空洞之意，但更强调形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ritual plus -istic means 'in the manner of a rite'.
normal.cn: ritual 加 -istic 意为「以仪式的方式」。

normal.en: The suffix -istic also builds artistic, characteristically and simplistic.
normal.cn: 后缀 -istic 还构成 artistic、characteristically 与 simplistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: ritualistic behavior, ritualistic gesture, ritualistic precision.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：仪式化行为、仪式性手势、仪式般的精确。

normal.en: The family runs rite, ritual, ritualistic, ritualism, ritualize and ritualization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rite、ritual、ritualistic、ritualism、ritualize 与 ritualization。

normal.en: The word is neutral in church history and critical in psychology.
normal.cn: 这个词在教会史中是中性的，在心理学中则带批评。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that repeats the same gesture until the gesture owns the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手重复同一个手势，直到手势反过来支配了手。

abstract.en: Picture a stage where every step has been decided before the music starts.
abstract.cn: 想象一个舞台，音乐未起，每一步都已被决定。

abstract.en: Picture a form that keeps standing after the meaning has left the room.
abstract.cn: 想象意义离开房间后，形式仍站在原地。

examples.en: The anthropologist noted the ritualistic greeting used at every door.
examples.cn: 人类学家记录了每道门前使用的仪式化问候。

examples.en: His ritualistic cleaning calmed him but exhausted his family.
examples.cn: 他仪式化的清洁让他安心，却让家人疲惫。

examples.en: The film's ritualistic pace divided the audience.
examples.cn: 影片仪式化的节奏让观众分成两派。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ritual（仪式）+ istic（……式的）」——像仪式一样的、按套路来的

root: 英语 ritual（来自拉丁 ritus「仪式」与 ritualis「与仪式有关的」）加后缀 -istic（经拉丁来自希腊 -istikos「以……方式」）。ritus 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one stylistic move: an action is performed as a rite, and that manner is then read as precision, faithfulness, compulsion, art, procedure, empty form and animal display.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个风格化动作展开：一个动作被当作仪式来完成，这种完成方式再依次被读作精确、虔诚、强迫、艺术、流程、空洞形式与动物展示。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand repeating one gesture until the gesture seems to belong to something older than the person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手重复同一个手势，直到这手势仿佛属于比人更古老的东西。

branches.en: THE MANNER: the adjective begins as a description of style, not of belief.
branches.cn: 方式：这个形容词起初描述风格，而非信仰。

branches.en: FIXITY, PRAISED OR BLAMED: the same exactness can look faithful or mechanical.
branches.cn: 固定性，或被赞或被责：同一种精确既可能显得虔诚，也可能显得机械。

branches.en: THE CAGE: when anxiety drives the repetition, the rite becomes a symptom.
branches.cn: 牢笼：当焦虑驱动重复，仪式就变成症状。

branches.en: STAGE AND EMPTY FORM: art borrows the rite's weight, and empty procedure borrows only its shell.
branches.cn: 舞台与空壳：艺术借来仪式的重量，空洞程序只借来外壳。

branches.en: PROCEDURE AND SIGNAL: organizations and animals both repeat a fixed sequence to make a message visible.
branches.cn: 流程与信号：组织与动物都重复固定序列，让讯息可见。

intro.en: Ritualistic is a Latin stem with two layers of suffix, one Latin and one Greek, and the same stem builds the whole ritual family.
intro.cn: ritualistic 是一个拉丁词干加两层后缀，一层拉丁、一层希腊，同一词干构成整个 ritual 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ritus and ritualis supply the stem; Greek -istikos, taken into Latin as -isticus, supplies the ending of manner.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ritus 与 ritualis 提供词干；希腊 -istikos 经拉丁作 -isticus，提供表方式的后缀。

items.example: The stem names the ceremony behind the manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干指方式背后的典礼。

items.example: Ritual is the base of the longer adjective.
items.exampleCN: ritual 是更长形容词的基础。
这个后缀构成表方式的形容词。

items.meaning: in the manner of a rite
items.example: The adjective describes how, not why.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述「如何」，不描述「为何」。

items.example: Ritualism names the tendency behind the manner.
items.exampleCN: ritualism 指方式背后的倾向。

items.example: The verb names the act of turning routine into rite.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把日常程序变成仪式。

items.example: Ritualization is the process the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: 仪式化正是这个形容词所描述的过程。

items.example: Rite is the shortest member of the family.
items.exampleCN: rite 是这个词族中最短的成员。

items.example: The adverb modifies the performance itself.
items.exampleCN: 副词修饰的是表演本身。

definition_en: to compare texts carefully and put them in order; to gather and arrange information
core_image: 两份手稿并排摊开，一页页比对
scene: 编辑把两份手稿逐页核对。 The editor collated the two manuscripts page by page.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：collate 指核对校勘；句意是编辑把两份手稿逐页核对。

senses.title: To compare texts carefully
senses.definition: to compare copies of a text to find and record differences
senses.definitionCN: 比对文本副本以找出并记录差异
senses.example: Scholars collated the three editions.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们校勘了三个版本。

senses.title: To gather and arrange
senses.definition: to collect information and put it in a clear order

senses.example: She collated the survey results into one table.
senses.exampleCN: 她把调查结果汇总成一张表。
senses.why: A comparison of pages became an organising job.
senses.whyCN: 比对页码变成了整理工作。

intro.en: Collate means to bring pages together for comparison.
intro.cn: collate 意为把页面带到一起作比较。

items.en: Con means together.
items.cn: con 意为一起。

items.en: Latus is the past participle of ferre, to carry.
items.cn: latus 是 ferre（携带）的过去分词。

items.en: Collatum means brought together.
items.cn: collatum 意为被带到一起。

items.en: Collate names the comparing of manuscripts.
items.cn: 十六世纪 collate 指校勘手稿。

items.en: The verb now covers gathering data too.
items.cn: 现代该动词也指汇总数据。

entries.definition: To bring things together.

entries.definitionCN: 碰撞。

entries.definition: To look for differences.

entries.definition: To collect material into one work.

entries.definition: To bring things into one place.

normalIntro.cn: collate 就是收集加比较：先把页带到一起，再核对。

normal.en: Col means together.

normal.en: Latus means carried.

normal.en: Carry the pages together.

abstract.en: Two books talking to each other.

abstract.en: Pages looking for their place.

abstract.en: Order made by comparison.

branches.en: Two editions compared line by line.

latus 产生 translate 与 relate。

definition_zh: 集市；市场；（观念、产品）竞争与交易的场所；线上交易平台
definition_en: an open area where goods are sold, or any setting in which goods, services or ideas compete for buyers
core_image: 广场上一排布棚，摊主把菜摆成整齐的堆，买的人在两排摊位之间来回比较
scene: 周末的广场上，摊主支起布棚，买菜的人挤在鱼摊前讨价还价。 The marketplace opens at six, when farmers bring in whatever survived the frost.
sceneCN: 这里 marketplace 指「摊贩聚集、公开买卖的露天场所」（第 1 个义项：作为实体的集市广场）；句意为集市六点开门，农夫把霜后剩下的东西都运来。

pos.zh: 集市；市场（可数）；竞争场所

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 mercatus（交易、市场）→ 市场；推销
market + -ing → 营销（语义偏移：从场所转到活动）
market 的缩略 → 集市（旧用法）
super-（在上）+ market → 超市（语义偏移：从露天场到自选店）

senses.title: An open square where stalls sell
senses.definition: a public open area where traders set up stalls and buyers come to buy
senses.definitionCN: 商贩摆摊、买者前来采购的公共露天场地
senses.example: The marketplace opens at six, when farmers bring in whatever survived the frost.
senses.exampleCN: 集市六点开门，农夫把霜后剩下的东西都运来。
senses.why: Market came from Latin mercatus 'trade, market', and place from Latin platea 'broad street', so the compound is literally a trading square.
senses.whyCN: market 来自拉丁 mercatus「交易、市场」，place 来自拉丁 platea「宽阔的街」，因此这个复合词字面上就是一块交易广场。

senses.title: The world of commercial competition
senses.definition: the abstract arena in which firms compete for customers, as in enter the marketplace
senses.definitionCN: 企业争夺顾客的抽象场域，如「进入市场」
senses.example: A new brand cannot survive long in a crowded marketplace.
senses.exampleCN: 新品牌在拥挤的市场里撑不了多久。
senses.why: The physical square stands for the whole arena where buyers can be won or lost.
senses.whyCN: 实体的广场代表整个可能赢得或失去买主的场域。

senses.title: An online platform for buying and selling
senses.definition: a website or app where many sellers list goods and many buyers purchase them
senses.definitionCN: 许多卖家挂货、许多买家下单的网站或应用
senses.example: The marketplace takes a commission on every sale.
senses.exampleCN: 这个平台对每笔交易抽取佣金。
senses.why: The square is rebuilt in software: stalls become listings, and the crowd becomes traffic.
senses.whyCN: 广场在软件里被重建：摊位成了商品页，人群成了流量。

senses.title: A place reserved for one trade
senses.definition: a building or area given over to one kind of dealing, as a fish market or a flower market
senses.definitionCN: 专供某一类买卖的建筑或区域，如鱼市、花市
senses.example: The fish marketplace behind the harbour starts work at three.
senses.exampleCN: 港口后面的鱼市三点就开始干活。
senses.why: One commodity can claim a whole square, and the compound follows the same pattern as market.
senses.whyCN: 一种货品就能占满一整块场地，复合词与 market 遵循同一模式。

senses.title: The available demand for a product
senses.definition: the set of buyers willing to purchase a particular product, treated as a place to be found
senses.definitionCN: 愿意购买某产品的买者整体，被当作一个可被找到的场所
senses.example: The device found a marketplace among rural clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 这种设备在农村诊所找到了市场。
senses.why: Demand is spoken of spatially: you enter it, find it, or are pushed out of it.
senses.whyCN: 需求被空间化地表述：你进入它、找到它，或被挤出它。

senses.title: A town's right to hold a market
senses.titleCN: 城镇举办集市的特许权
senses.definition: historical: the charter right of a town to hold a regular market, with tolls and rules
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：城镇定期举办集市、收取通行税并立规矩的特许权
senses.example: The charter granted the marketplace and the tolls that came with it.
senses.exampleCN: 特许状授予集市本身，以及随之而来的通行税。
senses.why: A market was a legal privilege before it was a location, so the word can mean the right itself.
senses.whyCN: 集市在被当作地点之前先是一项法律特权，因此这个词也可指权利本身。

senses.title: An arena of public argument
senses.definition: figuratively, a setting where ideas or claims are offered and weighed by an audience
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指各种主张被提出并由受众权衡的场域
senses.example: The letters page became a marketplace for rival histories.
senses.exampleCN: 读者来信版成了相互竞争的史观的集市。
senses.why: If buyers choose among goods, readers choose among arguments, and the same word serves.
senses.whyCN: 若买主在货物间挑选，读者便在论点间挑选，同一个词便可用。

senses.title: A platform business model
senses.definition: an attributive use marking businesses that host transactions rather than own stock
senses.definitionCN: 定语用法，标出撮合交易而不自持库存的企业
senses.example: Marketplace lending bypasses the branch and the teller.
senses.exampleCN: 平台型借贷绕过了支行与柜员。
senses.why: The noun becomes a classifier for a model, showing how far a word for a square can travel.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词变成一种模式的分类语，显示一个指广场的词能走多远。

intro.en: Both halves of marketplace are Latin borrowings, one for trade and one for a broad street, and the compound labels something older than either word.
intro.cn: marketplace 的两半都是拉丁借词，一半指交易，一半指宽阔的街；而这个复合词所标的事物比这两个词都古老。

items.en: Mercatus meant 'trade, traffic' and also 'a market', built on mercari 'to trade' and merx 'goods'. English market came from this noun through Germanic intermediaries.
items.cn: mercatus 意为「贸易、往来」，也指「市场」，建于 mercari「交易」与 merx「货物」之上。英语 market 经日耳曼语中介自这个名词而来。

items.en: Old English market is a borrowing from Latin mercatus, taken during the period of trade with the continent, so English has the Latin word twice, once directly and once through Germanic.
items.cn: 古英语 market 是从拉丁 mercatus 借来的，发生于与大陆贸易的时期；因此英语两次得到这个拉丁词，一次直接、一次经日耳曼语。

items.en: Place comes from Latin platea 'broad street', itself borrowed from Greek plateia (hodos) 'wide way', from platys 'broad'.
items.cn: place 来自拉丁 platea「宽阔的街」，而拉丁语又借自希腊 plateia (hodos)「宽路」，出自 platys「宽的」。

items.en: Old French place meant an open space or a square in a town, the sense English needs for the second half of the compound.
items.cn: 古法语 place 指城镇中的空地或广场，正是英语构成这个复合词后半所需之义。

items.en: Marketplace appears in English in the sixteenth century, when a town square with stalls needed a name distinct from market as an abstract trade.
items.cn: marketplace 于十六世纪出现在英语中，当时带摊位的城镇广场需要一个与抽象贸易义的 market 相区别的名称。

items.en: In the twenty-first century the compound is applied to online platforms, where no square exists but the same choosing among sellers takes place.
items.cn: 到二十一世纪，这个复合词被用于线上平台：那里没有广场，但同样的在卖家之间做挑选仍在上演。

note.en: The first group shares a half or a short form; the second holds words for places and systems of exchange.
note.cn: 第一组共享一半或一个短形式；第二组是交易场所与交易体系的其他说法。

entries.definition: The first element alone can mean trade in general, demand for a product, or a country region; only the compound insists on a physical square.
entries.definitionCN: 只取第一个成分时可泛指贸易、某产品的需求或某一国别市场；只有复合词才坚持指实体广场。

entries.definition: The second element alone means any location or a seat; it carries no trading sense by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 只取第二个成分时指任何地点或座位，本身不含交易义。

entries.definition: An old shortening of market, now mostly in names such as Wal-Mart or in historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: market 的旧缩略，今多用于沃尔玛这类名称或历史写作中。

entries.definition: The work of promoting goods, formed on market but naming an activity rather than a place.
entries.definitionCN: 推广货品的工作，由 market 构成，但指活动而非场所。

entries.definition: A market of many small stalls, often covered and in a region from North Africa to South Asia; it stresses the rows of shops.
entries.definitionCN: 由许多小摊构成的市场，常有顶棚，见于北非至南亚；强调成排的店铺。

entries.definition: An Arab market of narrow lanes, where each trade may occupy its own street.
entries.definitionCN: 阿拉伯世界由窄巷构成的市场，往往一种行业占一条街。

entries.definition: A market held at intervals, often with entertainment; the word stresses the occasion rather than the place.
entries.definitionCN: 定期举办、常带娱乐的市场；强调时机而非地点。

entries.definition: A formal venue or system for trading particular assets, such as a stock exchange; it has rules but no stalls.
entries.definitionCN: 交易特定资产的正式场所或体系，如证券交易所；有规则但无摊位。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: market 'trade' + place 'broad street': the street where trade happens.
normal.cn: market「交易」+ place「宽街」：交易发生的那条街。

normal.en: The family runs market, marketplace, marketing, marketer, marketable, supermarket, mart.
normal.cn: 同族词有 market、marketplace、marketing、marketer、marketable、supermarket、mart。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the widening: open-air marketplace, online marketplace, the marketplace of ideas.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出扩展：露天集市、线上市场、观念的市场。

normal.en: The compound needs a square; the short word does not: enter the market, but stand in the marketplace.
normal.cn: 复合词要求一块广场，短词不要求：进入市场，但站在集市里。

normal.en: The old law sense survives: a charter could grant a marketplace and its tolls.
normal.cn: 旧的法律义仍存：特许状可授予集市及随之的通行税。

abstract.en: Picture two rows of stalls with a narrow lane between them, and every choice made in that lane.
abstract.cn: 想象两排摊位之间一条窄道，所有选择都在这条窄道上做出。

abstract.en: Picture the same square rebuilt as a screen, with listings where cabbages used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象同一块广场被重建成一块屏幕，原来摆白菜的位置换成了商品页。

abstract.en: Picture a letters page where three historians bid for the same reader.
abstract.cn: 想象一个读者来信版，三位史家在那里争夺同一位读者。

examples.en: The marketplace empties by noon, when the ice under the fish has melted.
examples.cn: 到中午冰化成水，集市便空了。

examples.en: Small farmers sell through a marketplace that takes eight percent of every sale.
examples.cn: 小农通过一个抽取每笔交易百分之八的平台卖货。

examples.en: The university press put the book into a crowded marketplace with no advertising budget.
examples.cn: 这家大学出版社把书投进一个拥挤的市场，却没有广告预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: market（买卖）+ place（地方）＝ 买卖发生的那块地；先想露天的棚，再想屏幕里的货架。

root: market 来自拉丁 mercatus「贸易、市场」（经日耳曼语进入古英语）；place 来自拉丁 platea「宽阔的街」，再溯至希腊 plateia hodos「宽路」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a square to a business model: the open stalls, the arena of competition, the online platform, the single-trade hall, the demand to be found, the charter right, the arena of argument, and the platform classifier.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一块广场走到一种商业模式：露天摊位、竞争场域、线上平台、单一行业场所、可被找到的需求、特许权、论辩场域，以及平台分类语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rows of stalls with a lane between them, and a buyer walking that lane twice before choosing.
core.cn: 核心意象：两排摊位之间一条窄道，买主在那条道上走两遍才决定。

branches.en: A SQUARE AND A SPECIALITY: the general open market, then one commodity claiming a hall of its own.
branches.cn: 广场与专营：先是综合的露天市场，再是一种货品占据自己的场馆。

branches.en: MARKET AS ARENA: competition and demand are the square made abstract enough to enter and leave.
branches.cn: 作为场域的市场：竞争与需求就是被抽象到可以进出的一块广场。

branches.en: SOFTWARE AND MODEL: the platform rebuilds the stalls and then becomes a way of doing business.
branches.cn: 软件与模式：平台重建了摊位，随后本身成了一种做生意的方式。

branches.en: A RIGHT BEFORE A PLACE: a charter can create the market by granting it.
branches.cn: 先有权利后有地点：特许状可以靠授予来造出集市。

branches.en: BUYERS OF ARGUMENTS: ideas are weighed by readers the way goods are weighed by shoppers.
branches.cn: 论点的买主：观念被读者权衡，正如货物被顾客权衡。

intro.en: Marketplace is two borrowed nouns compounded, and each half has produced a family of its own in English.
intro.cn: marketplace 是两个借来的名词复合而成，每一半在英语里都各自衍生出一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin mercatus 'trade, market' supplies market, marketing and marketable; Latin platea 'broad street' supplies place, replace and placement. Greek plateia stands behind platea.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mercatus「交易、市场」给出 market、marketing、marketable；拉丁 platea「宽街」给出 place、replace、placement。希腊 plateia 是 platea 的来源。

items.example: The first element can stand alone as noun or verb.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分可独立作名词或动词。

items.example: The second element supplies the ground.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供那块地面。

items.example: The element recurs in workplace and showplace.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分在 workplace 与 showplace 中重现。

items.example: The compound fixes the abstract word to ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把抽象的词固定在地面上。

items.example: The suffix turns a place into an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把场所变成活动。

items.example: The person form follows the usual agent pattern.
items.exampleCN: 人称形式遵循常见的施动模式。

items.example: The suffix marks what a market will accept.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出市场会接受什么。

items.example: The prefix raises the scale of the square.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀抬高了广场的规模。

items.example: The place root also builds verbs of position.
items.exampleCN: place 词根也构成表位置的动词。

items.example: The clipping survives in trade names.
items.exampleCN: 这一缩略形式留存于商号名称中。

definition_zh: v. 传播；散布（信息、观念）；播撒
definition_en: to spread information, ideas or seeds widely to many people or places
core_image: 一只手把印好的纸张撒满整张大桌；风把种子从一块地带到许多块地；一个被吹空进空气里的蒲公英头
scene: 一只手把印好的纸张撒满整张大桌。 The agency disseminates the findings to every region.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：机构把研究结果发到每个地区，让尽可能多的人看到。

senses.title: Spread information
senses.definition: to spread information widely so that many people receive it
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把信息广泛传开，让许多人收到
senses.example: The agency disseminates the findings to every region.
senses.exampleCN: 机构把研究结果传播到每个地区。
senses.why: A hand scattering printed sheets across a wide table.
senses.whyCN: 一只手把印好的纸张撒满整张大桌。

senses.title: Spread ideas
senses.definition: to spread ideas or knowledge among many people
senses.definitionCN: （动词）在许多人之间传播观念或知识
senses.example: Teachers disseminate new methods.
senses.exampleCN: 教师们传播新方法。
senses.why: Seed carried on wind from one plot to many.
senses.whyCN: 风把种子从一块地带到许多块地。

senses.title: Scatter seed
senses.definition: to scatter seed or spores widely, the literal original sense
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把种子或孢子广泛撒开，即字面原义
senses.example: The wind disseminates the spores.
senses.exampleCN: 风把孢子播撒开去。
senses.why: A dandelion head emptied into the air.
senses.whyCN: 一个被吹空进空气里的蒲公英头。

intro.en: Disseminate comes from Latin disseminare, to scatter seed, from dis- plus seminare, to sow, from semen, seed; the word still carries the picture of sowing, now applied to information.
intro.cn: disseminate 来自拉丁语 disseminare「撒播种子」，由 dis- 加 seminare「播种」组成，源自 semen「种子」；这个词至今带着播种的画面，只是对象换成了信息。

items.en: Latin semen means seed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 semen 意为种子。

items.en: Seminare meant to sow.
items.cn: seminare 意为播种。

items.en: Disseminare meant to scatter seed abroad.
items.cn: disseminare 意为把种子撒向四处。

items.en: English disseminate is used for spreading abroad.
items.cn: 英语 disseminate 用于表示四处传布。

items.en: The word becomes common for spreading news and ideas.
items.cn: 这个词常用于传播新闻与观念。

items.en: Dissemination is the standard term for online distribution.
items.cn: dissemination 成为网络分发的标准用语。

note.en: Disseminate is sowing abroad; its look-alikes share the seed root, and its neighbours name other ways of getting something to many places.
note.cn: disseminate 是向四处播种；形近词共用种子词根，近义词则是别的把东西送到许多地方的方式。

definition_zh: n. 封锁；封锁部队；障碍物；v. 封锁；堵塞
definition_en: the sealing off of a place to stop goods or people moving in or out
core_image: 铁链横锁港口，商船尽数折返
scene: 海军舰队一字排开，铁链锁住了港湾出口。 The navy imposed a blockade on the enemy coast.
sceneCN: 这里 blockade 是名词「封锁」（第 1 个义项：以武力切断往来）；句意是海军对敌方海岸实施了封锁。

derivatives.zh: blockade 加 runner 的复合词，义为「突破封锁者」

senses.title: Sealing off a coast or port by force
senses.definition: the use of ships or troops to stop movement in or out of an area
senses.definitionCN: 以舰船或军队切断一地的进出
senses.example: The navy imposed a blockade on the enemy coast.
senses.exampleCN: 海军对敌方海岸实施了封锁。
senses.why: A block is anything that stops movement; -ade makes the stopping into an action.
senses.whyCN: block 指一切阻隔之物，后缀 -ade 把阻隔化为行动。

senses.title: The force carrying out the blockade
senses.definition: the ships or troops stationed to enforce a blockade
senses.definitionCN: 驻守以执行封锁的舰船或部队
senses.example: The blockade seized three ships trying to slip out.
senses.exampleCN: 封锁部队截获了三艘试图溜出的船。
senses.why: The action names the actors who carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 行动之名转指执行行动之人。

senses.title: A physical barrier blocking a road
senses.definition: a barrier placed to block a road, street, or passage
senses.definitionCN: 阻断道路或通道的障碍物
senses.example: Protesters built a blockade of burning tyres.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议者用燃烧的轮胎筑起路障。
senses.why: Block in its concrete sense of a heavy mass supplies the object.
senses.whyCN: block 的「大块实体」本义提供了障碍之物象。

senses.title: Stopping supplies in war or dispute
senses.definition: cutting off food, fuel, or trade to force surrender
senses.definitionCN: 切断粮食、燃料或贸易以迫降
senses.example: The blockade starved the city into surrender.
senses.exampleCN: 封锁令该城饥饿而降。
senses.why: Sealing the exits seals the stomach; the siege logic is ancient.
senses.whyCN: 封住出口即封住肠胃，围困之理自古如此。

senses.title: A commercial embargo
senses.definition: a legal or political bar on trade with a place
senses.definitionCN: 对某地贸易的法律或政治禁阻
senses.example: The blockade on exports ruined the plantation economy.
senses.exampleCN: 出口封锁令种植园经济崩溃。
senses.why: Trade is traffic like any other; stopping it is a block in another lane.
senses.whyCN: 贸易亦如车流，禁断贸易即另一条车道上的阻隔。

senses.title: To seal off with a blockade
senses.definition: to surround a place with forces so nothing passes
senses.definitionCN: 以兵力围困一地使其无法通行
senses.example: Rebel forces blockaded the capital for months.
senses.exampleCN: 叛军对首都实施了数月封锁。
senses.why: The noun made a verb, as actions so often become commands.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词，行动之名变为行动之令。

senses.title: To obstruct passage or progress
senses.definition: to block movement, plans, or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 阻隔通行、计划或谈判
senses.example: Medical aid was blockaded at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 医疗援助在边境受阻。
senses.why: Any stopping wall, of steel or of rules, is a block.
senses.whyCN: 无论是钢铁还是规章，凡阻隔之墙皆为 block。

senses.title: A physiological blockage
senses.definition: a medical stoppage, such as a nerve or vessel block
senses.definitionCN: 神经或血管等在医学上的阻断
senses.example: A nerve blockade relieved the surgical pain.
senses.exampleCN: 神经阻滞缓解了术后疼痛。
senses.why: The body has its own roads; stopping one is a block of the same kind.
senses.whyCN: 身体自有道路，阻断其一即为同义之 block。

definition_zh: 核能；原子核释放的能量；核能发电；核工业
definition_en: energy released from atomic nuclei, especially as electricity generated by nuclear reactors
core_image: 一颗极小的核被打开或合并，放出的热把一整片水变成蒸汽，蒸汽再推动巨大的叶片
scene: 这个国家的电表里，有三分之一来自原子核。 The country now draws a third of its electricity from nuclear energy.
sceneCN: 这里 nuclear energy 指「原子核释放并被用来发电的能量」（第 1 个义项：核裂变或核聚变释放的能量）；句意：这个国家如今有三分之一的电力来自核能。图中可辨识物件：反应堆厂房、冷却塔、电网、仪表盘。

senses.title: Energy released from atomic nuclei
senses.definition: the energy set free when heavy nuclei split or light nuclei combine
senses.definitionCN: 重核裂开或轻核结合时释放出来的能量
senses.example: A gram of uranium yields more nuclear energy than a tonne of coal.
senses.exampleCN: 一克铀释放的核能超过一吨煤。
senses.why: The nucleus holds its parts together with enormous force, and releasing those parts releases the energy that kept them bound.
senses.whyCN: 原子核以极大的力把各部分束缚在一起，松开这些部分便放出原本维系它们的能量。

senses.title: Electricity from reactors
senses.definition: the electrical power produced when reactor heat drives turbines
senses.definitionCN: 反应堆的热驱动汽轮机所产生的电力
senses.example: Nuclear energy supplies a large share of the grid at night.
senses.exampleCN: 核能在夜间为电网提供很大一部分电力。
senses.why: Heat from fission is turned into steam and then into current, so the phrase also names the product at the socket.
senses.whyCN: 裂变产生的热先变成蒸汽再变成电流，因此这个短语也指插座上的那个产品。

senses.title: The industry and its policy
senses.definition: the sector of companies, regulators and programmes that build and run nuclear plants
senses.definitionCN: 建造与运营核电站的企业、监管机构与计划所构成的部门
senses.example: The debate over nuclear energy divides the parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 围绕核能的争论使议会分裂。
senses.why: An energy source that requires huge capital becomes an institution, and the phrase shifts from physics to politics.
senses.whyCN: 一种需要巨额资本的能源会成为制度，于是这个短语从物理滑向政治。

senses.title: The binding energy inside the nucleus
senses.definition: the energy stored in the bonds between nucleons, measurable as the mass the nucleus lacks
senses.definitionCN: 储存在核子之间、可通过核所缺的质量测出的能量
senses.example: The binding energy of iron is at the peak of the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 铁的结合能正处在曲线的顶点。
senses.why: Mass and energy are interchangeable, and the missing mass of a nucleus is exactly the nuclear energy that would be needed to take it apart.
senses.whyCN: 质量与能量可以互换，而核所缺的那部分质量，正是把它拆开所需的核能。

senses.title: The energy of a nuclear weapon
senses.definition: the explosive energy released by an uncontrolled fission or fusion reaction
senses.definitionCN: 不受控的裂变或聚变反应放出的爆炸能量
senses.example: The first test proved that nuclear energy could be released in an instant.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次试验证明核能可以在一瞬间释放。
senses.why: The same binding energy, released slowly in a reactor, becomes a blast when released at once.
senses.whyCN: 同样的结合能，在反应堆里缓慢释放便是电力，一次性释放便成爆炸。

senses.title: The power that lights the stars
senses.definition: the energy produced by fusion inside stars, including the sun
senses.definitionCN: 恒星内部、包括太阳内部由聚变产生的能量
senses.example: All sunlight is nuclear energy arriving from the core.
senses.exampleCN: 所有阳光都是来自太阳核心的核能。
senses.why: Stars run on the same nuclear reactions, so the phrase names the source of daylight as well as of electricity.
senses.whyCN: 恒星靠同样的核反应运转，因此这个短语既指日光的来源，也指电力的来源。

senses.title: The older name for the same thing
senses.definition: the historical label atomic energy, used before the nucleus was understood as the source
senses.definitionCN: 历史上的「原子能」说法，在人们弄清能量源于原子核之前使用
senses.example: Old textbooks speak of atomic energy where new ones say nuclear energy.
senses.exampleCN: 旧教科书说「原子能」，新教科书则说「核能」。
senses.why: The atom was the known unit when the effect was discovered, so the older name credited the whole atom rather than its centre.
senses.whyCN: 发现这一效应时，原子是已知的单位，因此旧名把功劳记在整个原子上，而不是它的中心。

senses.title: The heat inside the Earth
senses.definition: the geothermal heat produced by the decay of radioactive isotopes in the planet's interior
senses.definitionCN: 行星内部放射性同位素衰变所产生的地热
senses.example: Nuclear energy keeps the mantle warm enough to move.
senses.exampleCN: 核能使地幔保持足以流动的温热。
senses.why: Decay releases energy continuously, and over billions of years that trickle has become a planetary furnace.
senses.whyCN: 衰变持续放出能量，数十亿年下来，这点滴之热成了一座行星熔炉。

intro.en: Nuclear energy joins nuclear, from Latin nucleus 'kernel, nut', to energy, from Greek energeia 'activity'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nuclear energy 把源于拉丁 nucleus「果仁、核」的 nuclear 接到源于希腊 energeia「活动」的 energy 上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nux, nucis meant 'nut'. The small hard kernel inside supplied the image of a compact centre.
items.cn: nux 意为「坚果」。里面那颗小而硬的仁，提供了「紧密中心」的意象。

items.en: The diminutive nucleus meant 'a little nut, a kernel', and Latin writers already used it for the core of a thing.
items.cn: 指小形式 nucleus 意为「小坚果、果仁」，拉丁作者已用它指某物的核心。

items.en: Energeia meant 'activity, working', built from en 'in' and ergon 'work'. Latin borrowed it as energia.
items.cn: energeia 意为「活动、运作」，由「在内」与「工作」构成。拉丁语借入为 energia。

items.en: As the cell nucleus and later the atomic nucleus were named, the kernel image moved from biology to physics.
items.cn: 随着细胞核、后来又随原子核被命名，果仁的意象从生物学移到了物理学。

items.en: The phrase nuclear energy spread as reactors and weapons showed that the nucleus stores vast energy.
items.cn: 反应堆与武器显示核内储存巨大能量之后，「核能」这一说法传播开来。

items.en: The first uses of the exact phrase are approximate; both source words are fully attested.
items.cn: 这个确切短语最早的使用年代为约数；两个来源词都有完整书证。

note.en: Group one holds nut-root look-alikes; group two holds names for the same energy measured in other ways.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「坚果」词根的形近词；第二组是从其他角度称呼同一种能量的说法。

entries.definition: The bare adjective meaning 'of the nucleus'; it describes weapons, reactors and medicine as well as energy.
entries.definitionCN: 指「原子核的」的形容词；它除能量外也修饰武器、反应堆与医学。

entries.definition: The central body of an atom or cell; the energy is named after the object that stores it.
entries.definitionCN: 原子或细胞的核心体；能量以储存它的那个对象命名。

entries.definition: From the same kernel-root: relating to the nucleus of a cell, as in nucleic acid, with no connection to reactors.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「核」词根：指细胞核的，如核酸，与反应堆无关。

entries.definition: The everyday English word from the same ancient root; the scientific nucleus began as a little nut.
entries.definitionCN: 与那个古老词根同源的日常英语词；科学上的「核」原本就是一颗小坚果。

entries.definition: The pre-1940s label for the same power; it credited the whole atom before the nucleus was known to be the source.
entries.definitionCN: 二十世纪四十年代以前对同一种动力的称呼；在弄清核才是来源之前，它把功劳记在整个原子。

entries.definition: Usually the electrical output or the industry; nuclear energy is the broader physical and political term.
entries.definitionCN: 通常指电力产出或这个行业；而「核能」这一说法则是更宽泛的物理与政治用语。

entries.definition: The precise measure of the energy that holds a nucleus together; it explains where nuclear energy comes from.
entries.definitionCN: 维系原子核的能量之精确度量；它解释了核能从哪里来。

entries.definition: The spontaneous emission of rays; it is one route by which nuclear energy appears as heat.
entries.definitionCN: 自发放出的射线；它是核能以热的形式出现的一条途径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin nucleus 'kernel' plus Greek energeia 'activity': the activity of the kernel.
normal.cn: 拉丁「果仁」加希腊「活动」：果仁的活动。

normal.en: The family runs nuclear energy, nuclear, nuclear power, nuclear reactor, nuclear-free.
normal.cn: 同族表达包括核能、核的、核电、核反应堆、无核的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: nuclear energy plant, nuclear energy policy, civil nuclear energy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：核能电站、核能政策、民用核能。

normal.en: The old name atomic energy credited the whole atom; the new name credits its kernel.
normal.cn: 旧名「原子能」把功劳记在整个原子，新名则记在它的果仁。

normal.en: The same binding energy is slow heat in a reactor and instant blast in a weapon.
normal.cn: 同一份结合能，在反应堆里是缓慢的热，在武器里是一瞬的爆。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny stone that can boil an entire lake.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗小石头能烧开整片湖。

abstract.en: Picture a nut whose shell holds a whole winter of warmth.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗果壳里装着整个冬天的暖。

abstract.en: Picture a star and a power station lit by the same small fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗恒星与一座电站由同一点小火点亮。

examples.en: Nuclear energy produces no carbon dioxide while running.
examples.cn: 核能在运行时不产生二氧化碳。

examples.en: The country expanded nuclear energy after the oil crisis.
examples.cn: 石油危机之后，这个国家扩大了核能。

examples.en: Some of the Earth's internal heat is nuclear energy from decaying isotopes.
examples.cn: 地球内部的一部分热来自同位素衰变产生的核能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nuclear（核的）+ energy（能量）」——原子核里放出的能量，就是核能

root: nuclear（拉丁 nucleus「果仁、核」，为 nux「坚果」的指小形式）+ energy（希腊 energeia「活动」= en「在内」+ ergon「工作」）。英语 nuclear energy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the released binding energy to the electricity, the industry, the stored quantity itself, the weapon, the star, the older name and finally the planet's internal heat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从释放的结合能走到电力、行业、被储存的量本身、武器、恒星、旧称，最后是行星内部的热。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kernel opened or joined, and its heat turning water into steam that drives great blades.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗核被打开或合并，它的热把水变成蒸汽，蒸汽推动巨大的叶片。

branches.en: THE SOURCE: the energy released and the energy stored are the same quantity before and after the bond is broken.
branches.cn: 来源：被放出的能量与被储存的能量，是键被打开前后的同一个量。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: heat becomes current, and current becomes an industry with rules and budgets.
branches.cn: 体系：热变成电流，电流又变成一个带规则与预算的行业。

branches.en: THE TWO EXTREMES: released at once it is a blast, released steadily in a star it is daylight.
branches.cn: 两个极端：一次性放出是爆炸，在恒星里稳定放出则是日光。

branches.en: THE OLD LABEL: the earlier name credited the whole atom before the kernel was understood.
branches.cn: 旧标签：早先的名字在弄清核之前把功劳记在整个原子。

branches.en: THE DEEP FURNACE: the slow decay of isotopes keeps the planet's interior warm.
branches.cn: 深处熔炉：同位素的缓慢衰变使行星内部保持温热。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Latin kernel word with a Greek word for working, a typical scientific mixture.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语的「果仁」与希腊语的「运作」配对，是典型的科学混合造词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nucleus and nux also yield nuclear, nucleic and nut; Greek energeia came into Latin as energia and then into English as energy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nucleus 与 nux 还衍生出 nuclear、nucleic 与 nut；希腊 energeia 进入拉丁语成为 energia，再进入英语成为 energy。

items.example: The hard shell protects a small kernel.
items.exampleCN: 硬壳保护着里面的小仁。

items.example: The diminutive names the core of a thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个指小形式指某物的核心。

items.example: Nuclear forces hold the protons together.
items.exampleCN: 核力把质子维系在一起。

items.example: The word names work being done.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指正在被做的工作。

items.example: Energy is stored in the bonds of the nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 能量储存在原子核的键里。

items.example: Nuclear energy is released in reactors.
items.exampleCN: 核能在反应堆中被释放。

items.example: The reactor turns heat into steam.

latinEntries.structure: energia, energiae (f., first declension, from Greek energeia)

definition_zh: 线粒体的；与线粒体有关的；由线粒体编码、介导或定位的
definition_en: relating to a mitochondrion, or produced, encoded, controlled or located within mitochondria
core_image: 一个细胞器被虚线框住，框线上贴着写有「属于它」的标签，框内的部件都染上同一种颜色
scene: 这里指「线粒体的」。 Mitochondrial DNA passes from mother to child, so it traces a single maternal line.
sceneCN: 这里 mitochondrial 指「线粒体自有的（由线粒体基因组编码的）」（第 3 个义项：由线粒体 DNA 编码或存在于其中的）；因此线粒体 DNA 只沿母系传递。图中可辨识物件：虚线框、标签、环状 DNA、母系箭头。

pos.zh: 线粒体的；与线粒体相关的（通常不作定语以外的名词用）

senses.title: Belonging to the organelle
senses.definition: relating to or belonging to a mitochondrion
senses.definitionCN: 属于线粒体或与线粒体有关的
senses.example: Mitochondrial proteins are made partly in the cytosol and partly inside the organelle.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体蛋白一部分在细胞质中制造，一部分在细胞器内制造。
senses.why: the suffix -al turns the organelle's name into a label of belonging, so the adjective begins as a simple possessive.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把细胞器的名称变成表示归属的标签，因此这个形容词的起点只是一个简单的所属关系。

senses.title: Located inside the organelle
senses.definition: situated or occurring inside mitochondria
senses.definitionCN: 位于线粒体内部或在线粒体内发生的
senses.example: Mitochondrial calcium uptake shapes the organelle's response to stress.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体对钙的摄取塑造了该细胞器对压力的反应。
senses.why: once a thing has a boundary, the adjective can also mark where an event happens, not only whom it belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物有了边界，这个形容词也能标记事件发生的位置，而不只是所属关系。

senses.title: Encoded by the organelle's own genome
senses.titleCN: 线粒体编码的：自身基因组来源
senses.definition: encoded by the small genome carried inside mitochondria rather than by the nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 由线粒体内部携带的小基因组编码，而不是由细胞核编码
senses.example: Only thirteen proteins in humans are fully mitochondrial.
senses.exampleCN: 人类只有十三种蛋白质完全由线粒体基因编码。
senses.why: the organelle turned out to hold its own instructions, so 'mitochondrial' came to mark origin of code as well as place.
senses.whyCN: 该细胞器被发现自带指令，于是 mitochondrial 除了地点，也开始标记「编码来源」。

senses.title: Inherited through the mother
senses.titleCN: 母系遗传的：沿卵细胞传递
senses.definition: passed down through the maternal line because mitochondria travel in the egg, not the sperm
senses.definitionCN: 因线粒体随卵细胞而非精子传递，故沿母系向下遗传
senses.example: Mitochondrial inheritance explains why affected mothers pass the trait to all children.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体遗传解释了为何受累母亲会把该性状传给所有子女。
senses.why: because the genome sits outside the nucleus, its inheritance rule is separate, and the adjective names that route.
senses.whyCN: 因为这份基因组在核外，其遗传规则自成一套，这个形容词命名的正是那条路径。

senses.title: Of disease caused by organelle failure
senses.titleCN: 线粒体病的：由细胞器功能障碍引起
senses.definition: describing disease that arises from faulty mitochondrial function or genome
senses.definitionCN: 描述由线粒体功能或基因组缺陷引发的疾病
senses.example: Patients with mitochondrial disease often show muscle weakness first.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体病患者常先出现肌无力。
senses.why: when the power plant fails, the whole body suffers, so the adjective attaches to a clinical category.
senses.whyCN: 当发电厂出故障，全身都会受损，于是这个形容词附着在一个临床类别上。

senses.title: Of the membranes and their potential
senses.titleCN: 线粒体膜的：膜与膜电位
senses.definition: relating to the organelle's membranes, especially the inner membrane and its electrical potential
senses.definitionCN: 与线粒体膜相关，尤其指内膜及其电位
senses.example: A fall in mitochondrial membrane potential is an early sign of damage.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体膜电位下降是损伤的早期信号。
senses.why: the adjective narrows from the whole organelle to its two skins, because that is where the electrical work happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从整个细胞器收窄到它的两层皮，因为电学工作正发生在那里。

senses.title: Targeted to the organelle
senses.titleCN: 靶向线粒体的：研究与药物用语
senses.definition: describing a probe, drug or signal that is deliberately directed to mitochondria
senses.definitionCN: 描述被有意导向线粒体的探针、药物或信号
senses.example: The team designed a mitochondrial antioxidant to reach the matrix.
senses.exampleCN: 团队设计了一种线粒体抗氧化剂以进入基质。
senses.why: research practice adds a purposive sense: the adjective now marks a destination chosen by a designer.
senses.whyCN: 科研实践加入了一层目的义：这个形容词现在标记一个由设计者选定的目的地。

senses.title: The cell's energetic core, figuratively
senses.titleCN: 引申义：细胞能量核心的
senses.definition: used figuratively for whatever supplies the driving energy of a system
senses.definitionCN: 引申指任何为系统提供驱动能量的事物
senses.example: The city's mitochondrial role is played by its port.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市里扮演「线粒体」角色的是它的港口。
senses.why: as the organelle stands for energy supply itself, the adjective can be borrowed for any source of power.
senses.whyCN: 当这个细胞器本身就是能量供应的代名词，这个形容词便可借指任何动力来源。

intro.en: Mitochondrial is the English adjective on mitochondrion, with the Latin suffix -alis; the base is a Greek compound coined in 1898.
intro.cn: mitochondrial 是以 mitochondrion 为词干、加拉丁后缀 -alis 构成的英语形容词；词干是 1898 年创造的希腊合成词。

items.en: mitos 'thread' plus chondrion 'small granule' produced mitochondrium; the adjective inherits that compound unchanged.
items.cn: mitos「线」加 chondrion「小颗粒」产生 mitochondrium；形容词原样继承这个合成词。

items.en: Latin -alis formed adjectives of relation, as in naturalis from natura. English keeps it as -al, so mitochondrion gives mitochondrial.
items.cn: 拉丁 -alis 构成表示关系的形容词，如 natura 变 naturalis。英语保留为 -al，于是 mitochondrion 变 mitochondrial。

items.en: New Latin mitochondrium is a Latinized spelling, not an inherited word; no classical Latin root can be claimed for the base.
items.cn: 新拉丁语 mitochondrium 是拉丁化拼写，不是传承词；不应为该词干主张古典拉丁词根。

items.en: The adjective appears in English cytology in the early twentieth century, soon after the noun; the first citation is approximate.
items.cn: 该形容词于 20 世纪初随名词进入英语细胞学文献；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Work on mitochondrial genetics in the mid-twentieth century fixed the senses 'encoded by' and 'inherited through the mother'.
items.cn: 20 世纪中期的线粒体遗传学研究固定了「由……编码」与「经母系遗传」两个义项。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation of the adjective is not recorded, and its derivational order relative to the noun is also unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该形容词的最早英语书证无确切记录；其与名词的派生先后亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the same stem but differ in part of speech or in the organelle named; group two holds adjectives that answer a similar question about location or cause.
note.cn: 第一组是共享词干、但词性或所指细胞器不同的词；第二组是回答相同位置或来源问题的形容词。

entries.definition: The organelle itself, a count noun. Use it where a thing is meant, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞器本身，是可数名词；需要指事物而非性质时用它。

entries.definition: Cell division named from thread-like chromosomes; same Greek piece, entirely different process.
entries.definitionCN: 因染色体呈线状而得名的一种细胞分裂；希腊构件相同，所指过程完全不同。

entries.definition: A cartilage cell. Sharing chondros 'cartilage' does not make it an organelle word.
entries.definitionCN: 软骨细胞；虽共享 chondros「软骨」，仍与细胞器无关。

entries.definition: Means 'at the level of mitochondria' and modifies a verb or adjective; it cannot modify a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「在线粒体层面」，修饰动词或形容词，不能修饰名词。

entries.definition: Located in the cytoplasm, that is, outside the organelle; it is the contrasted location, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 位于细胞质，即细胞器之外；它是相对立的位置，而非同义词。

entries.definition: Relating to organelles in general. Mitochondrial specifies which organelle, so the two differ in precision.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与细胞器相关；mitochondrial 指明是哪一个细胞器，二者精确度不同。

entries.definition: Inside a cell but not tied to any one compartment; it is a wider location word.
entries.definitionCN: 在细胞内，但不限于某一区室；是范围更宽的位置词。

entries.definition: Describes a process that needs oxygen. Mitochondrial respiration is aerobic, but the words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 描述需要氧的过程；线粒体呼吸是有氧的，但两词回答的不是同一个问题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mitochondrion + -al: the '-al' is the same relational suffix as in natural and structural.
normal.cn: mitochondrion + -al：这个 -al 与 natural、structural 中的关系后缀相同。

normal.en: The family runs mitochondrion, mitochondria, mitochondrial, mitochondrially, mitochondriopathy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mitochondrion、mitochondria、mitochondrial、mitochondrially、mitochondriopathy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mitochondrial DNA, membrane potential, dysfunction, biogenesis, inheritance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：线粒体 DNA、膜电位、功能障碍、生成、遗传。

normal.en: Clinical use is easy to recall because the organelle's failure weakens muscle first.
normal.cn: 临床用法好记，因为该细胞器出故障时最先受累的是肌肉。

normal.en: The -al adjective answers 'whose?', 'where?' or 'made by whom?', and the context picks one.
normal.cn: 这个 -al 形容词回答「谁的」「在哪」「由谁制造」，由上下文选定其中之一。

abstract.en: Picture a dashed box drawn around one organelle, with everything inside tinted the same colour.
abstract.cn: 想象给一个细胞器画上虚线框，框内一切染成同一种颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a factory with its own small rulebook, separate from the city's law book.
abstract.cn: 想象一座工厂自带一本小规则书，与城市的法典分开。

abstract.en: Picture a power source so central that other buildings are named after the energy they draw from it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个动力源如此核心，以至于其他建筑都以它们从中获取的能量来命名。

examples.en: Mitochondrial proteins must cross two membranes to reach the matrix.
examples.cn: 线粒体蛋白要穿过两层膜才能到达基质。

examples.en: Exercise increases mitochondrial biogenesis in trained muscle.
examples.cn: 运动会使受训肌肉的线粒体生成增加。

examples.en: The drug was designed to spare mitochondrial function.
examples.cn: 该药被设计为不损害线粒体功能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「线粒体（mitochondrion）加个 -al」——凡贴上线粒体标签的 → 线粒体的、线粒体内的

root: 希腊 mitos「线」+ chondrion「小颗粒」→ 新拉丁 mitochondrium（1898）→ 英语名词 mitochondrion + 拉丁关系后缀 -alis → mitochondrial。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one possessive suffix: a thing belongs to the organelle, then lies inside it, is coded by it, is inherited through it, is diseased through it, is specified to its membranes, is aimed at it, or finally stands for energy itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个表所属的后缀散开：先属于该细胞器，再位于其内、由其编码、经其遗传、因其而病、具体到其膜、被有意指向它，最后甚至代指能量本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dashed boundary drawn around one organelle, tinting everything inside as 'its'.
core.cn: 核心意象：围绕一个细胞器画出的虚线边界，把其中一切都染成「它的」。

branches.en: POSSESSION: the plainest reading, a label of belonging attached by -al.
branches.cn: 所属：最朴素的读法，即由 -al 附上的归属标签。

branches.en: LOCATION: the boundary also marks where an event takes place.
branches.cn: 位置：边界同时标记事件发生的地点。

branches.en: ORIGIN OF CODE AND ROUTE: the organelle's own genome and the maternal path it travels.
branches.cn: 编码来源与传递路径：细胞器自有基因组，以及它沿母系传递的路径。

branches.en: FAILURE: when this boundary malfunctions, the adjective names a clinical category.
branches.cn: 故障：当这条边界失灵，该形容词命名一个临床类别。

branches.en: NARROWING AND EXTENDING: from the two membranes, to a chosen target, to any source of power.
branches.cn: 收窄与外扩：从两层膜，到被选定的靶点，再到任何动力来源。

intro.en: The adjective is a Greek scientific stem plus the Latin relational suffix -alis; the suffix does the grammatical work.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由希腊科学词干加拉丁关系后缀 -alis 构成；语法工作由后缀承担。

latinIntro.en: No inherited Latin base exists; only the suffix -alis is Latin, and New Latin mitochondrium is a re-spelling of the Greek compound.
latinIntro.cn: 没有传承的拉丁词干；只有后缀 -alis 属拉丁语，新拉丁语 mitochondrium 只是希腊合成词的改写。

items.example: Mitochondrial membranes are rich in cardiolipin.
Each mitochondrion has its own genome.
items.exampleCN: 每个线粒体都有自己的基因组。

items.example: Mitochondria divide independently of the cell cycle.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体可独立于细胞周期分裂。

items.example: Mitochondriopathy affects tissues that need much energy.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体病影响高耗能组织。

items.example: Cold exposure stimulates mitochondriogenesis in fat.
items.exampleCN: 寒冷刺激会促进脂肪中的线粒体生成。

items.example: Mitochondrial DNA has few repair enzymes.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体 DNA 的修复酶很少。

items.meaning: the inner compartment of the organelle
items.example: The matrix holds the enzymes of the citric acid cycle.
items.exampleCN: 基质容纳三羧酸循环的酶。

latinEntries.meaning: womb; a mould; the ground substance

definition_zh: 子午线；经线；正午；顶点；经络
definition_en: a great circle through the poles, especially one used as a longitude reference, or the moment of midday
core_image: 太阳在天空升到最高，一条从南到北划过天顶的隐形大圆正好对着它
scene: 正午时分测量杆的影子缩到最短。 At noon the sun crosses the meridian and the shadow reaches its shortest.
sceneCN: 这里 meridian 指「过南北两极、也过天顶的大圆」（第 7 个义项：观测者所在的天球子午圈）；句意为太阳经过这条大圆时正当正午，杆影最短。图中可辨识物件：测量杆、影子、太阳、南北方向的标线。

senses.title: A great circle through the poles
senses.titleCN: 子午线：过南北两极的大圆
senses.definition: a great circle on the earth passing through both poles and any given place
senses.definitionCN: 地球上过南北两极与某地的大圆
senses.example: Every place lies on its own meridian.
senses.exampleCN: 每个地方都位于自己的一条子午线上。
senses.why: Latin meridies meant 'midday'; the sun at noon lies on the north-south circle, so that circle became the meridian.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 meridies 意为「正午」；正午太阳位于南北向的圈上，这条圈因此被称为子午线。

senses.title: The prime meridian
senses.titleCN: 本初子午线：经度计数的零度线
senses.definition: the meridian chosen as zero longitude, internationally fixed at Greenwich
senses.definitionCN: 被选作零度经线的子午线，国际上定在格林尼治
senses.example: Longitude is counted east and west from the prime meridian.
senses.exampleCN: 经度从本初子午线向东、向西计数。
senses.why: One meridian must be chosen as the zero for all others, and that choice is a convention rather than a natural line.
senses.whyCN: 必须选一条子午线作为其它经线的零点，这个选择是约定而非天然界线。

senses.title: Midday or noon
senses.titleCN: 正午：太阳位于当地最高点的时间
senses.definition: the time of day when the sun is at its highest point, that is, local noon
senses.definitionCN: 太阳位于当地最高点的时间，即当地正午
senses.example: The ceremony took place at the meridian.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式在正午举行。
senses.why: Meridian comes straight from meridies 'midday', so the word can still name the hour itself, not only the line.
senses.whyCN: meridian 直接来自 meridies「正午」，因此这个词仍可指这个时刻本身，而不只是线。

senses.title: The sun's highest point
senses.titleCN: 太阳中天：太阳到达当日最高处的时刻
senses.definition: the moment when the sun reaches its greatest altitude and crosses the observer's meridian
senses.definitionCN: 太阳达到当日最大高度并经过观测者子午圈的时刻
senses.example: The astronomers recorded the meridian of the sun with a transit instrument.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家使用中星仪记录了太阳中天的时刻。
senses.why: The crossing of the meridian is the physical event that defines noon, so 'meridian' names both the line and the crossing.
senses.whyCN: 经过子午圈是定义正午的物理事件，因此 meridian 既指线也指这次经过。

senses.title: The peak of achievement
senses.titleCN: 顶点：事业或成就的最高处
senses.definition: the highest point of success, fame or a career
senses.definitionCN: 成功、名声或事业的最高点
senses.example: The composer was at his meridian when he wrote the symphony.
senses.exampleCN: 作曲家写这部交响曲时正处于创作顶峰。
senses.why: The sun at noon is at its highest, so the same word pictures any career at its high point.
senses.whyCN: 正午的太阳升到最高，同一个词便用来比喻任何事业的最高点。

senses.title: An acupuncture channel
senses.titleCN: 经络：中医里气血运行的通道
senses.definition: one of the channels in traditional Chinese medicine along which qi and blood are said to flow
senses.definitionCN: 中医认为气血运行的通道之一
senses.example: The acupuncturist traced a meridian down the patient's arm.
senses.exampleCN: 针灸师沿着病人手臂的一条经络施针。
senses.why: English translators needed a word for these channels and borrowed 'meridian', because a channel runs like a line across the body.
senses.whyCN: 英语译者需要为这些通道找词，便借用了 meridian，因为经络像一条线贯穿身体。

senses.title: The observer's celestial meridian
senses.titleCN: 天球子午圈：过天顶与天极的大圆
senses.definition: the great circle on the celestial sphere passing through the poles and the observer's zenith
senses.definitionCN: 天球上过天极与观测者天顶的大圆
senses.example: Stars rise and culminate on the celestial meridian.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星在天球子午圈上升起并达到中天。
senses.why: The zenith and the two celestial poles define one great circle, and observers track stars as they cross it.
senses.whyCN: 天顶与两个天极确定一条大圆，观测者就在恒星越过它时进行追踪。

senses.title: Meridian passage or transit
senses.titleCN: 中天：天体经过子午圈的时刻
senses.definition: the passage of a celestial body across the observer's meridian
senses.definitionCN: 天体经过观测者子午圈的时刻
senses.example: The planet's meridian was predicted for midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗行星的中天时刻被预测在午夜。
senses.why: Once the line is fixed, the event of crossing it needs a name too, so astronomy uses meridian for the transit.
senses.whyCN: 线固定之后，越过它的事件也需要名称，因此天文学用 meridian 指这次中天。

intro.en: Meridian comes from Latin meridianus 'of midday, southern', from meridies 'midday, south', itself from medius 'middle' and dies 'day'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: meridian 来自拉丁 meridianus「正午的、南方的」，源于 meridies「正午、南方」，而 meridies 由 medius「中间」与 dies「日」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Medius meant 'middle'; it marks the centre of the day, the point where the sun stands highest.
items.cn: medius 意为「中间的」；它标出一天的中心，也就是太阳最高之处。

items.en: Dies meant 'day'; its deeper origin is connected with a root for brightness, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: dies 意为「日、白天」；其更深来源与表示明亮的词根相关，属重构形式而非有记录的词。

items.en: Medius plus dies produced meridies, 'midday, and by extension the south', since the sun at noon stands toward the south in the northern hemisphere.
items.cn: medius 加 dies 构成 meridies，意为「正午」，并引申为「南方」，因为北半球正午太阳位于南方。

items.en: Meridianus meant 'of midday or of the south'; this adjective passed through French and became the English noun meridian.
items.cn: meridianus 意为「正午的、南方的」；这个形容词经法语演变为英语名词 meridian。

items.en: English meridian appears in the fourteenth century for noon and for the north-south line; the geographical reference sense developed in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
items.cn: 英语 meridian 在 14 世纪出现，指正午与南北方向的线；作为经度参考的用法在 16 至 17 世纪发展起来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the acupuncture sense is a modern translation choice, and its exact first English use is not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：经络义属现代翻译选择，其在英语中的确切首见年代未见记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like meridian; group two holds the lines, times and peaks it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是外形接近 meridian 的词；第二组是容易与它混淆的线、时刻与顶点概念。

entries.definition: From medius 'middle': the middle value in a set or a line through a midpoint, with no noon meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 medius「中间」：一组数的中间值或过中点的线，不含正午义。

entries.definition: The middle size or a means of communication; it shares medius but not the day.
entries.definitionCN: 指中等尺寸或媒介；同出 medius，但与「日」无关。

entries.definition: The adjective from meridian in its 'south' sense: southern, or running north-south.
entries.definitionCN: 由 meridian 的「南方」义变来的形容词：南方的，或南北走向的。

entries.definition: An uncommon variant spelling of meridional; standard usage prefers meridional.
entries.definitionCN: meridional 的罕见异体拼写；标准用法多用 meridional。

entries.definition: The east-west angle measured from a meridian; a meridian is the line, longitude is the number.
entries.definitionCN: 相对某子午线量出的东西角度；meridian 是线，longitude 是数值。

entries.definition: A latitude circle running east-west; it crosses meridians at right angles.
entries.definitionCN: 东西走向的纬线圈，与子午线正交。

entries.definition: The middle of the day, when the sun is highest; meridian can name the same moment formally.
entries.definitionCN: 一天的正中、太阳最高之时；meridian 可正式地指同一时刻。

entries.definition: The point directly overhead, or figuratively the peak; the meridian passes through it.
entries.definitionCN: 头顶正上方的点，或比喻的顶点；子午圈经过它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin 'middle day', real navigation and real astronomy, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「一日之中」、真实的航海与真实的天文学，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Medius 'middle' + dies 'day': midday, then the north-south line the noon sun crosses.
normal.cn: medius「中间」+ dies「日」：正午，再指正午太阳经过的南北向线。

normal.en: A meridian runs north-south; longitude is counted east and west from one chosen meridian.
normal.cn: 子午线南北走向；经度从选定的那条本初子午线向东西计数。

normal.en: Ante meridiem and post meridiem are the Latin phrases behind a.m. and p.m.
normal.cn: ante meridiem 与 post meridiem 就是 a.m. 与 p.m. 背后的拉丁短语。

normal.en: The sun culminates, or crosses the meridian, at local noon.
normal.cn: 太阳在当地正午达到中天，也就是经过子午圈。

normal.en: Acupuncture meridians are channels, a metaphorical line running through the body.
normal.cn: 针灸经络是通道，像一条穿过身体的比喻之线。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow shrinking to nothing as the sun stands overhead.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳当顶时影子缩到几乎没有。

abstract.en: Picture a career that has reached its noon and can only move sideways.
abstract.cn: 想象一项事业已到正午，此后只能横向移动。

abstract.en: Picture a seam down the middle of a sphere, joining both ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从球体正中穿过、连接两端的接缝。

examples.en: The prime meridian passes through Greenwich.
examples.cn: 本初子午线穿过格林尼治。

examples.en: The ship's chronometer was set to the meridian of Greenwich.
examples.cn: 船上的航海钟按格林尼治子午线设定。

examples.en: His career reached its meridian in the 1990s.
examples.cn: 他的事业在二十世纪九十年代达到顶点。

dict_mnemonic.text: meri（中间，如 medium）+ dian（日，如 diary 每日）→ 一日之中 → 正午、子午线

root: 拉丁 meridies「正午、南方」= medius「中间」+ dies「日」；meridianus「正午的、南方的」经法语进入英语，兼指正午与南北向大圆。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from 'middle of the day': the north-south line the noon sun crosses, the zero line chosen for longitude, the hour of noon, the sun's culmination, the peak of a career, the body's channels, the sky's north-south circle, and the transit across it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「一日之中」出发：正午太阳经过的南北线、被选作经度零点的线、正午时刻、太阳中天、事业顶点、身体通道、天球南北圈，以及越过它的事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the noon sun standing on an invisible north-south circle that runs through both poles and the observer's zenith.
core.cn: 核心意象：正午的太阳立在一条看不见的南北大圆上，这条圆穿过两极与观测者天顶。

branches.en: THE LINE: the earth and the sky each draw the same north-south great circle.
branches.cn: 线：地球与天空各自画出同一条南北大圆。

branches.en: ZERO BY AGREEMENT: one meridian is chosen as the zero for all the others.
branches.cn: 约定的零度：选一条子午线作为其余各线的零点。

branches.en: THE MOMENT: noon, the sun's culmination and the star's transit are the same crossing seen as time.
branches.cn: 时刻：正午、太阳中天与恒星中天，是同一次穿越在时间上的呈现。

branches.en: THE PEAK: a career at its height is the noon sun applied to a life.
branches.cn: 顶点：事业的高处，就是正午太阳用于人生。

branches.en: THE BODY: a channel running through the body borrows the line's shape.
branches.cn: 身体：贯穿身体的通道借用了线的形态。

intro.en: Meridian is built from Latin words for 'middle' and 'day'; the same parts survive in midday, medius and the a.m./p.m. phrases.
intro.cn: meridian 由拉丁的「中间」与「日」两个词构成；同样的成分保存在 midday、medius 与 a.m./p.m. 短语中。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius 'middle' and dies 'day' combine in meridies 'midday'; meridies yields meridianus and the English meridian, while medius also gives median and medium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 medius「中间」与 dies「日」组合成 meridies「正午」；meridies 衍生 meridianus 与英语 meridian，而 medius 还衍生 median 与 medium。

definition_zh: 桦树；桦木；桦条（旧时体罚用具）；用桦条抽打
definition_en: a slender tree with pale bark; a rod made of its twigs; to whip with such a rod
core_image: 白皮修长的桦树，枝条也曾被扎成戒尺
scene: 白皮树在风里沙沙作响，落叶铺满小径。 The old schoolmaster kept a birch in the closet.
sceneCN: 这里 birch 是「桦条（旧时体罚用具）」（第 3 个义项：用桦枝扎成的笞具）；句意是老校长在柜子里备着一束桦条。

derivatives.zh: birch 加形容词后缀，义为「桦木的；桦树多的」
同源近亲词，义为「山毛榉」，与 birch 同出古代树名

senses.title: A slender tree with pale bark
senses.definition: a tree of cold regions with smooth pale bark and thin branches
senses.definitionCN: 寒带树种，树皮光滑色浅，枝条纤细
senses.example: The old schoolmaster kept a birch in the closet.
senses.exampleCN: 老校长在柜子里备着一束桦条。
senses.why: The Old English name for the tree, related to an ancient root for bright, for its shining bark.
senses.whyCN: 古英语树名，或与表示「明亮」的古词根相关，指其树皮发亮。

senses.title: The wood of the birch
senses.definition: the hard pale wood of the birch tree
senses.definitionCN: 桦树的浅色硬木
senses.example: The cabinet was made of solid birch.
senses.exampleCN: 这口柜子用整块桦木制成。
senses.why: Tree-names pass easily to their timber.
senses.whyCN: 树名常转指其木材。

senses.title: A bundle of birch twigs for flogging
senses.definition: a bunch of birch twigs formerly used to whip offenders
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用桦枝扎成、用于抽打犯错者的笞具
senses.example: Boys feared the birch more than detention.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩们更怕桦条而非留堂。
senses.why: Flexible birch twigs made the traditional school rod.
senses.whyCN: 柔韧的桦枝是传统的校用戒具。

senses.title: To whip with a birch
senses.definition: to flog someone with a bundle of birch twigs
senses.definitionCN: 以桦枝束抽打某人
senses.example: Sailors were once birched for small faults.
senses.exampleCN: 水手曾因小过被桦条抽打。
senses.why: The instrument names the punishment.
senses.whyCN: 刑具之名转为刑罚之名。

senses.title: Birch bark and its uses
senses.definition: the papery bark used for canoes, baskets, and writing
senses.definitionCN: 如纸般的树皮，用于造船、编篮与书写
senses.example: Native craftworkers sewed birch into canoes.
senses.exampleCN: 原住民工匠把桦皮缝成独木舟。
senses.why: The bark is the tree's most useful part.
senses.whyCN: 树皮是桦树最有用的部分。

senses.title: Birch as scenery
senses.definition: birch trees as a feature of landscape and literature
senses.definitionCN: 作为风景与文学意象的桦树
senses.example: Silver birches lined the northern road.
senses.exampleCN: 白桦夹道立于北方的路上。
senses.why: Pale trunks make birches a painter's tree.
senses.whyCN: 浅色树干使桦树成为画家之树。

senses.title: The birch as institution
senses.definition: corporal punishment by birch as a legal or school practice
senses.definitionCN: 作为法律或学校惯例的桦条体罚
senses.example: The birch was abolished in that country decades ago.
senses.exampleCN: 那个国家数十年前废除了桦条刑。
senses.why: The rod stands for the whole punishing institution.
senses.whyCN: 一束桦条代表整个体罚制度。

senses.title: Birch in folklore
senses.definition: the tree's place in seasonal customs and folklore
senses.definitionCN: 桦树在节庆与民俗中的角色
senses.example: Villagers hung birch sprigs at the spring festival.
senses.exampleCN: 村民在春庆时悬挂桦枝。
senses.why: Purifying, bright-barked trees collect folklore.
senses.whyCN: 树皮明亮、可作净化之用的树易聚民俗。

intro.cn: birch 是来源古老的古英语树名。

items.en: birce or beorc meant the birch tree.

items.cn: 中古英语 birche 兼指树、木材与笞条。

items.en: the verb to birch and the punishment the birch completed the family.
items.cn: 动词 birch 与刑罚 the birch 补全词族。

note.cn: 形近组汇集近形树名；近义组汇集笞打类词。
